display.purpose: The one page headline (hero, lab, proof wall). Class type-display.

head.purpose: Studio panel and fieldset headings. Class type-head.

body.purpose: Section prose in ink-2, 34 to 40rem measure.

label.purpose: Field names, slug entries, nav, captions, patch names, group headings. Never a kicker above a headline. Class type-label.

reading.purpose: Every measured value, in fixed rolling cells. Class type-reading.

mono.purpose: Hex entries and code identifiers only.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The system is flat. The only box-shadow is the inset ring pair on the range thumb (inset 0 0 0 4px sheet, inset 0 0 0 10px magenta), which draws a registration mark, not depth.

motion.name: ease-print
motion.purpose: Expo-out curve for plates pulling into register and readings rolling over.

motion.name: reading-roll
motion.value: 320ms ease-print, y -0.55em to 0 in, 0 to 0.55em out, 25ms stagger per cell
motion.purpose: Only changed character cells roll over.

motion.name: plate-register
motion.value: transform 900ms ease-print, delay 300ms + 140ms per plate; opacity 600ms, delay 1150ms + 120ms per plate
motion.purpose: Cyan, magenta and yellow plates arrive about 10px out of register on first view, then align and give way to the black.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.value: spring stiffness 520 damping 26; scale [1, 1.06, 1], rotate -2.5deg to 0; magenta fill held about 900ms; tap scale 0.95
motion.purpose: The stamp lands, inks and lifts on download.

motion.name: tab-rule
motion.purpose: The 3px active-tab rule slides between tabs.

motion.name: toggle-block
motion.purpose: The ink block slides to the side that is set.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"; CSS animation and transition durations 0.01ms; scroll-behavior auto
motion.purpose: Every motion has a still, registered end state.

motion.name: loading
motion.value: LazyMotion strict with domMax loaded by dynamic import after first paint
motion.purpose: The animation engine never blocks the first render.

components.css: .ds-strip{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(9.5rem,1fr));list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;border-left:1px solid var(--rule,#111);border-top:1px solid var(--rule,#111);background:var(--sheet,#fbfbf9);font-family:Archivo,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--ink,#111)}.ds-patch{position:relative;display:flex;flex-direction:column;border-right:1px solid var(--rule,#111);border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule,#111)}.ds-weakest{outline:2px solid var(--magenta,#e4007f);outline-offset:-4px}.ds-swatch{display:block;height:28px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule,#111)}.ds-gauge{display:block;height:28px;box-sizing:border-box;padding:6px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule,#111)}.ds-gframe{position:relative;display:block;height:100%;border:1px solid var(--hair,#c6c6bf);background:var(--sheet,#fbfbf9)}.ds-gfill{position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;left:0;background:var(--cyan,#00a0e9);transition:width .5s}.ds-plabel{padding:6px 8px 0;font-size:11.5px;font-weight:650;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-2,#4a4a45)}.ds-read{padding:0 8px 8px;font-size:17px;line-height:1.25;font-weight:700;font-stretch:92%;letter-spacing:-.01em;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-tag{position:absolute;top:6px;right:6px;padding:0 4px;background:var(--sheet,#fbfbf9);color:var(--magenta-ink,#c4006c);font-size:9.5px;font-weight:650;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase}

components.css: .ds-wedge{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(6,1fr);list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;border-left:1px solid var(--rule,#111);border-top:1px solid var(--rule,#111)}.ds-wedge li{position:relative;height:48px;border-right:1px solid var(--rule,#111);border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule,#111)}.ds-ok{background:var(--ink,#111)}.ds-no{background:var(--sheet,#fbfbf9);color:var(--magenta-ink,#c4006c)}.ds-no svg{position:absolute;inset:8px;width:calc(100% - 16px);height:calc(100% - 16px)}.ds-unk{background:var(--tint,#f0f0ec)}.ds-sel{outline:2px solid var(--magenta,#e4007f);outline-offset:-5px}

narrative.overview:
Every page is one tall proof sheet of bright coated stock lying in a light booth. It is set in black ink, carries printer's marks at its corners and trims, and keeps the three process inks for jobs: magenta marks what needs doing and what is wrong, cyan marks registration and information, and yellow is only ever a highlighter laid under black ink. The code being proofed is the only picture on the sheet. Content runs further down the same sheet and never onto a second one beside it.

The density is that of a job ticket: ruled tables with small-capital field names, live readings in fixed tabular cells, and heavy wide display type cut in at poster size. Depth, softness and decoration are absent by construction. A proof is flat, its corners are square, and anything that moves is behaving like print: plates pulling into register, a densitometer ticking over, a stamp landing.

Dark mode is the same sheet read as a film positive with the booth lamp off. Roles hold. Only values change.
keyCharacteristics: One sheet on a grey booth, with crop marks at the corners, a sticky slug line at its head and ruled section trims.
Ruled job-ticket grids (1px black rules, shared borders) instead of cards.
Archivo on its width axis: wide and heavy for display, condensed and tabular for readings.
Process inks as signals, never as decoration.
Flat, square, shadowless. The codes themselves are the only gradients.

rules.name: The Process Ink Rule
rules.body: Magenta means act or fault, cyan means registration or information, yellow means caution under black. An ink used only because it looks nice is a misprint.

rules.name: The Text-Safe Ink Rule
rules.body: Any magenta or cyan set as text or a stroke under 3px uses its `-ink` variant on light stock. The bright ink is for fills, outlines and patches.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Width comes from `font-stretch`, not from letter-spacing or a second family. Wide is for display, normal for labels, narrow for readings.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Code Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono sets hex entries and code identifiers, nothing else. Readings stay in Archivo.

rules.name: The Fixed Cell Rule
rules.body: Any value that changes in place is tabular, so that nothing beside it reflows.

rules.name: The Flat Proof Rule
rules.body: A proof is flat. Lift, glow, glass and blur are all off the sheet. To separate something, rule it off.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Nothing on a proof is rounded except the marks a printer draws round: registration targets and proofreader's rings.

dos: Do build every new surface as more of the same sheet. Gutters are 16/24/40px, section padding is 56px (80px at `lg`), and each section closes with a black rule.
Do group content in ruled job-ticket grids where cells share 1px rule lines, with small-capital field names in a fixed label column.
Do keep magenta for the primary action and for faults. Use magenta-ink whenever it is text or a thin stroke on light stock.
Do use cyan for focus (a 2px outline offset by 2px), registration and information gauges, and yellow only under black ink.
Do set every changing value as a Reading in tabular figures and fixed cells.
Do get width from Archivo's width axis: display at 110–115%, readings at 92%.
Do draw marks (crop, registration, proof marks) as hairline SVG with square caps.
Do give every animation a reduced-motion state that shows the finished, registered result.
donts: Don't add shadows, glass, blur or glows. Rule things off instead.
Don't use gradients outside the QR codes being proofed. The only other linear gradients are functional: the checkerboard and the scroll-edge mask.
Don't round corners. Circles are only for registration targets, the registration-mark thumb and proofreader's rings.
Don't put a small-capital label above a headline as an eyebrow or kicker. Small capitals name fields and groups. They never introduce a headline.
Don't use magenta, cyan or yellow decoratively, or let one stand in for another's role.
Don't wrap content in cards with fills, padding and radius. Use a ruled row or cell.
Don't set readings in JetBrains Mono, or set prose in it. It is for hex and code only.
Don't place a second sheet beside the first. Content continues down the sheet.
